title: PicoBB — BBC BASIC for the Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040 UART console)
expect: BBC BASIC for Pico Console v0.50

components.license: Zlib (PicoBB + BBCSDL) with bundled LittleFS and pico-sdk runtime (BSD-3-Clause)
components.source: built by fetch.sh: make BOARD=pico STDIO=UART SERIAL_DEV=0 SOUND=NONE (RP2040 console UART build)

picobb.role: Pico port of BBC BASIC (the thing built)

notes: PicoBB (Memotech-Bill), the Raspberry Pi Pico port of R. T. Russell's BBC BASIC (BBCSDL), built in its simplest console configuration: a UART console on RP2040. Build flags: BOARD=pico (RP2040, no CYW43 WiFi), STDIO=UART (console on UART0 only, no USB-CDC), SERIAL_DEV=0 (no extra serial device), SOUND=NONE, LFS=Y (LittleFS flash store), FAT=N, STACK_CHECK=4 (PicoBB's own stack_trap.c, so the custom-licensed m0FaultDispatch.c is NOT compiled in). Console I/O is pico-sdk stdio_uart on UART0 (PL011 @ 0x40034000, GP0/GP1, 115200 8N1) — the peripheral bw-board's rp2040js machine emulates. SOUND=NONE is required: the default SOUND=SDL launches core1, and bw-board's rp2040js adapter steps core0 only, so a core1 build hangs in the SIO inter-core FIFO handshake. This is NOT a runMediaBundle bundle: runMediaBundle has no rp2040 machine factory and its entry logic is 16-bit, so proof.mjs drives bw-board's canonical createRp2040jsAdapter() directly (the same adapter lite's probe-pico-micropython.mjs and bw-board's pico-blink test use): boot the UF2 from flash, capture UART0 TX via adapter.onSerial, type via rp2040.uart[0].feedByte. The console is an ANSI terminal: on start it waits for the user to press Enter (sends '.' each second until a CR arrives over UART), then queries terminal size with ESC[6n; proof.mjs answers those DSR queries like a VT100 (ESC[24;80R). On first boot LittleFS has no image, so PicoBB formats the flash store and continues to the '>' prompt. programs[] are scripted REPL sessions (input = bytes typed, expect = what the machine prints; BBC BASIC right-justifies numbers in a 10-char field, hence the leading spaces). Reproducibility: fetch.sh pins SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH to PicoBB's commit date so the firmware's build-date banner is deterministic; the one build-location-specific string (an absolute littlefs source path from a __FILE__) is stripped with -ffile-prefix-map, so the UF2 reproduces byte-for-byte on the same toolchain (arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.2, pico-sdk 2.1.1) regardless of build path; proof.mjs (behaviour) is the authoritative check.
